content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee: Donna Ball (E024), requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes conflict:
- HR note: full-time Payroll Specialist, recommends write for Source Code (within full-time limit write; admin only if role owns system — Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code, Engineer does).
- Security note: contractor with basic security training, max access is read. Contractor can get write only with advanced security training. So recommends read.

The policy: The maximum level an employee may have. Which note is correct? There's a discrepancy between HR and Security. Security DB says contractor with basic training. The safer/more conservative assessment seems to be the security note.

As Approver, I need to make the final decision. The conflicting facts: employment type differs. The access policy depends on employment type. Security note says contractor with basic training, max read. HR note says full-time, max write.

Which to trust? Typically the security note is authoritative for access. Given the conflict, granting read seems safest. The requested level is write, but maximum per security note is read. So grant read.

Let me decide: level = read, reason: conflicting employment info; security DB indicates contractor with basic training, max read. Grant read (maximum allowed).

I'll submit.
